title: Dynamic token-leasing scheduler for tenant isolation and latency hedging
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a dynamic token-leasing layer in the prefill/decode scheduler that grants short-lived "leases" of token processing capacity to tenants and request classes. Leases are sized using attention-cost projections and recent phase-duration statistics. The goal is to isolate tenant microbursts, reduce p99/p999 latency tails, and preserve throughput by allowing controlled reclamation and opportunistic consolidation. The system should provide weighted fairness, soft deadlines, and kernel-selection hints so the runtime can steer phases to optimized kernels when appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra (PM + 2 eng reviewers)
Benchmarked on staging: p99 latency reduced by >= 20% for noisy tenants without >5% throughput loss across mixed workload
Scheduler exposes per-tenant lease metrics and eviction events in Console (per-route breakdown)
Safe rollout plan (canary + automatic rollback) and integration tests covering lease reclamation and hedging under OOM/kernel-fallback scenarios
comments: 2026-02-26 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial proposal posted. Focused on token leases rather than static quotas to preserve short-term throughput. Linked estimator design.

2026-03-08 - Liam Chen: Added reclaim path to return unused lease tokens to pool and an opportunistic merge path that attempts to consolidate small leases to feed high-efficiency kernels. Pushed draft PR for scheduler changes.

implementation_notes: Core components: Lease Manager (fast path allocation + reclaim), Attention-Cost Estimator (per-request projection using prefill token-count and head-sparsity proxy), Broker/Arbiter (weighted fair assignment), Kernel Hint Interface (attach hints to phase descriptor), and Telemetry hooks (per-lease metrics: granted_tokens, used_tokens, reclaimed_tokens, eviction_count). Start with single-node scheduling experiment then expand to cross-shard coordination.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: over-aggressive reclamation causing request stalls. Mitigation: implement grace window + hedged re-lease attempt. Risk: estimator mis-sizing leading to unfairness. Mitigation: add short-term smoothing and automatic down-weighting for tenants with repeated misses.
next_steps: 1) Complete GH PR and run canary on staging for small tenant cohort. 2) Add console panels for per-lease telemetry. 3) Run cross-tenant fairness experiments with production traffic mirror. 4) Iterate estimator with kernel-cost feedback loop.
notes_for_oncall: Lease eviction events will surface as route-level 'evicted_tokens' metrics. If eviction spikes correlate with elevated kernel-fallbacks, revert canary and investigate estimator regression. Escalate to runtime-scheduler for persistent >10% p50 latency increase.
